title: Why Your Trading App Gets Paid When You Lose
alts: Your Trading App Is Free. So Who's Paying? (It's You)
Why Trading Apps Throw Confetti When You Lose Money
line1: Dave's free trading app felt like a game: confetti, notifications, swipe and tap. Three months later his $2,000 car fund was down to $400.
summary: Dave thought zero commission meant free. But his trading app made $1.1 billion last year from options trades alone—about 48 cents per contract. The app doesn't care if you win. It cares that you trade. This video follows the money: payment for order flow, why options pay the app almost 4x more than stocks, the hidden spread wholesalers earn, the gamification tactics (confetti after trades, constant notifications), and the one setting that saved Dave's last $400. We show the official numbers from annual reports and academic studies, explain why 97% of persistent day traders lose money, and walk through the five steps Dave used to turn off the parts of the app designed to keep him tapping. Education, not advice.
learn: What payment for order flow is and how trading apps sell your orders to wholesalers

How the bid-ask spread works and why small traders pay an average 12.6% gap on weekly options
Why gamification tactics (confetti, notifications) are designed to make you trade more, not win more
The Brazil study: 97% of persistent day traders lost money, with no evidence of learning
The five settings Dave changed to save his last $400: turn off options, kill notifications, move app off home screen, ask the no-confetti question, automate a boring index fund
